headline: A stormy, wet week: a stronger Pacific storm Wednesday night into Thanksgiving brings around an inch of rain to the Puget Sound lowlands, damaging-wind potential on the coast and north interior, and possible major coastal flooding along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines at Thanksgiving's high tides.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Rain from the first of a series of weather fronts spread inland early Tuesday, but a lull is likely later in the morning into the afternoon, especially away from the coast, before the front pushes onshore this evening for another round of rain. Winds stay gusty, strongest on the coast, where a Wind Advisory runs until 4 PM Tuesday for the north and Grays Harbor coasts and the western and southern Olympic foothills; elsewhere in the lowlands, including Seattle, expect southeast winds of about 5–15 mph with gusts to around 20 mph. A Winter Weather Advisory covers the Cascades of Whatcom and Skagit counties until 10 PM Tuesday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Any break in the rain and wind Wednesday will be brief as a stronger storm, driven by a powerful jet-stream wind core far offshore, heads in. Strong southeast winds could reach high-wind levels Wednesday night into early Thursday on the coast and across the North Interior. From Wednesday afternoon to Thursday afternoon, rain totals reach about an inch in the interior lowlands outside the Olympic rain shadow (the drier zone around Sequim and Port Angeles should see less), 2+ inches on the coast, 3–5 inches in the Olympics and 1.5–3 inches in the Cascades, with snow levels well above the mountain passes. A Flood Watch runs from Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon for the Olympics and their western and southern foothills, Olympia and southern Puget Sound, southern Hood Canal, the Chehalis Valley and the Willapa and Black Hills; the Skokomish River in Mason County will likely flood around midweek, reaching moderate and possibly near major levels, though no widespread river flooding is expected.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Confidence is only fair for Thursday night through the weekend. High pressure may build into California, but Western Washington sits too far north to get much benefit, as storms ride over the top of it into the area, so any weekend break will be brief. Computer models agree that another broad low-pressure pattern settles offshore early next week, bringing a return to more active, wet and windy weather as December arrives.

coast: High surf, low air pressure and some of the year's highest tides create the potential for major coastal flooding, peaking Wednesday on the Pacific coast and on Thanksgiving for inland shorelines. A Coastal Flood Warning runs from 8 AM to 3 PM Tuesday for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca (including the Sequim and Port Angeles shore) and the north and Grays Harbor coasts, until 4 PM for San Juan County, and a Coastal Flood Advisory runs until 5 PM Tuesday for Seattle, Everett, Island County, Pierce/south King, Skagit/Snohomish and Whatcom lowland shorelines. Coastal Flood Watches then cover the Strait of Juan de Fuca, Port Townsend, Puget Sound, Kitsap, Hood Canal, the San Juans and the outer coast from late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon and again from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. A High Surf Advisory covers the north and Grays Harbor coasts from 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM Wednesday, with seas of 18–22 feet through Friday, easing to 10–13 feet Friday and 6–8 feet Saturday before building back to 10–13 feet early next week. For boaters, storm-force gusts offshore (10–60 miles out) and gale-force gusts on the inner coastal waters and the Strait run through Tuesday evening, with gale warnings extended through Wednesday afternoon on the coastal waters and east Strait and a Small Craft Advisory for the west Strait; Thursday's front brings another round of potentially storm-force winds to the coastal waters and gales in the east Strait, with a reprieve Friday and rough to severe conditions on the Grays Harbor bar.
watch_for: Possible major coastal flooding at high tide along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines, peaking Thanksgiving Day.
High winds Wednesday night into early Thursday on the coast and in the North Interior.
Heavy rain in the Olympics and river rises, with the Skokomish River likely to reach moderate or near-major flood levels midweek.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in a wet, windy week with the strongest storm Wednesday night into Thursday, have only fair confidence in the details from Thursday night through the weekend, and are more confident in another active stretch starting early next week.
